//longRunningTestSeconds: BARCH-009. The test clients impose no wall-clock limit any more, so nothing interrupts a test that has genuinely stopped making progress. This is what replaces that: the runner reports any test still running after two minutes, repeatedly, by name. Two minutes is deliberately just above the 100-second HttpClient default that used to fail these tests, so the information the old timeout produced is not lost -- it is downgraded from a failure into a report, which is the right register for a number that is really a guess about how fast the machine is.
//diagnosticMessages: Required for longRunningTestSeconds to reach the output at all. It costs some discovery noise on every run, which is the price of a hang that names itself.
